clue.text: An Abigail not mass-produced we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells the solver that the spoken sound of a phrase is what matters here

parts.note: something not mass-produced is made by hand, handmade

explanation.surface: Someone describes a craft item as not factory-made, judging by what they hear.
explanation.walkthrough: An abigail is an old word for a lady's maid, from a waiting-gentlewoman in a 17th-century play; 'we hear' says HANDMADE is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: An abigail is a lady's personal maid, a female servant.

clue.text: Harsh bark causes trouble

parts.note: harsh means severe, hard
a bark (barque) is a sailing vessel, a ship

explanation.surface: A dog's rough barking causes problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bark' looks like a dog's noise but is a type of sailing vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardship is suffering or adversity, the difficulties of a tough life.

clue.text: Cook was one for planning courses

definitions.text: Cook was one for planning courses

parts.words: Cook was one for planning courses
parts.note: not a chef planning meal courses: Captain James Cook charted sea routes

explanation.surface: A chef who enjoyed devising the courses of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Cook was a famous explorer who plotted ships' routes at sea.

clue.text: Where whisky needs a lot of water all round

parts.note: malt is a kind of whisky

explanation.surface: A place where a whisky drinker needs plenty of water added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of water all round' looks like a drink being diluted, but describes an island, with 'Where' and 'needs' as links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean island nation is surrounded by sea.

clue.text: People dressed like Friar Tuck, say

explanation.surface: Folk wearing monkish robes like Robin Hood's friar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'People' is a verb, to populate; Friar Tuck, Robin Hood's monk companion, wears a habit, so the answer is also read as two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To people a place is to live in it, to occupy it; a friar in his robe is in his monastic garb.

clue.text: High cost of vessel

explanation.surface: The steep price charged for a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To cost a packet is British slang for a big price, and a packet boat is a ship carrying mail.

clue.text: Exotic dance a lot like Scheherazade's performance?

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange and foreign, so these letters are given an unfamiliar arrangement

explanation.surface: A foreign dance, very like the storyteller's act.
explanation.walkthrough: Scheherazade told stories night after night in The Arabian Nights, so her performance is story-based.
explanation.definitionFit: Scheherazade's act was telling tales, and anecdotal means consisting of short stories.

clue.text: Upset ink over Smith and Steel

indicators.note: in a down clue over means one piece is placed above the other
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word ink is read from the bottom up

parts.note: F. E. Smith, Lord Birkenhead, was a famous lawyer and politician

explanation.surface: Ink spilt over two people named Smith and Steel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reverses INK to KNI; 'over' puts it above FE (F. E. Smith, the British statesman).
explanation.definitionFit: Steel is used poetically for a blade or sword.

clue.text: Aggregates placed at foot of columns

explanation.surface: Sums written beneath the columns of figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Totals are sums; in accounts the sums are written below each column of figures.

clue.text: Refreshment with a kiss is all he needs

parts.note: ale is a refreshing drink
X represents a kiss
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man happy with a drink and a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'he' is the definition: a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexis is a boy's given name.

clue.text: Absolute match?

parts.note: Captain Absolute is a character in Sheridan's play The ..., so a match for him is one of the title figures, a competitor

explanation.surface: A query about a perfect pairing.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor is someone who matches another; Sheridan's Captain Absolute is one in The Rivals.

clue.text: This possibly includes female linguist

indicators.note: includes means one part is placed within the other
possibly says the four letters of the word this may be arranged another way

parts.note: Ellen is a female name

explanation.surface: A remark that this group perhaps has a woman language expert among it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' looks like the subject of the sentence but is the fodder for 'possibly'; 'includes' wraps it round the woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hellenist is a scholar of the Greek language and culture, a kind of language specialist.

clue.text: It controls, trains, and gives the go-ahead to fight

parts.note: to signal is to give a sign such as the go-ahead
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: Someone who regulates, coaches, and permits a boxing match.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'It controls, trains' as 'it controls trains': the commas break up the definition to mislead.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway building whose operator sets the points and lights that govern rail traffic.

clue.text: Duke fit to remain in House

parts.note: fit means healthy, well

explanation.surface: A healthy duke chooses to stay in his mansion.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to live or stay in a home.

clue.text: Commend another spell in confidence

explanation.surface: Someone praises a further period of being trusted.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a verb meaning commend or hand over, in the less usual of its two spellings ('another spell'); the second reads the answer as two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To commit something to someone's care is the old variant spelling of entrust; and something held on trust is held in confidence.

clue.text: Result of air force intake rising

parts.note: rising means going up
a draught is an intake of drink or air

explanation.surface: The Air Force's recruitment rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air force' looks like the RAF and 'intake' like recruits, but they mean moving air and a gulp.
explanation.definitionFit: An upward current of air is what a moving air mass produces.

clue.text: Lord of the Rings?

parts.note: not Tolkien's book: a planet famed for its rings, named after a Roman god, so a lord of rings

explanation.surface: A reference to Tolkien's fantasy epic.
explanation.definitionFit: The ringed sixth planet takes its name from the Roman god of agriculture, a ruling deity.

clue.text: Plan in outline for boisterous players

explanation.surface: Sketching out a scheme for a rowdy team.
explanation.definitionFit: A roughcast is a preliminary sketch or draft; read as two words, a rough cast is a rowdy group of actors.

clue.text: Distribution of hares

parts.note: read as an instruction, the answer says take SHARE and work it out, which rearranges it into the clue's hares

explanation.surface: How hares are spread across the land.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: 'share' with 'out' as a signal to shuffle its letters gives HARES.
explanation.definitionFit: A share-out is the dividing of something among people.

clue.text: Game involving characters in the news

definitions.text: Game involving characters in the news

parts.words: Game involving characters in the news
parts.note: the letters of the word news are N, E, W, S, the compass seats of the four players in a card game

explanation.surface: A pastime featuring celebrities from the headlines.
explanation.definitionFit: The card game is played by North, East, West and South, letters spelling news.

clue.text: Code variations

explanation.surface: Different versions of a secret cipher.
explanation.walkthrough: Enigma was the German cipher machine of World War II; Elgar's Enigma Variations is a famous orchestral work.
explanation.definitionFit: The Enigma was a wartime German cipher system; Elgar's orchestral set is the Enigma Variations.

clue.text: Sort of mace used to protect the young Moses

definitions.text: used to protect the young Moses

explanation.surface: A kind of weapon used to guard the infant prophet.
explanation.walkthrough: Reed mace is another name for this waterside plant; in Exodus the baby Moses was hidden in an ark made of it among the reeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Reedmace is a tall marsh plant also called cattail; the infant Moses was laid in a papyrus basket by the Nile.

clue.text: Square the difference

explanation.surface: Settle what separates two numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: To square an account is to settle it equally; a remainder owed in accounts is also called this.

clue.text: Type of bird — five in a cote perhaps

indicators.note: in means one letter is placed within the others
perhaps says the letters of a cote may form something else

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A bird type, with five of them living in a dovecote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges A COTE into AOCET, and 'in' puts V after the first A.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocet is a black-and-white wading bird with an upturned beak.

clue.text: A striking goddess

explanation.surface: An impressive deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A striking' means something you strike: a vesta is an old word for a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A vesta is a short match lit by striking; Vesta is also the Roman goddess of the hearth.

clue.text: Rocket motive force

parts.note: not a space rocket: Stephenson's Rocket was an early railway locomotive, driven by boiling water vapour

explanation.surface: What propels a rocket.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephenson's Rocket locomotive was powered by the vapour of boiling water.

clue.text: One who wants not to be a do gooder

definitions.text: One who wants not to be a do gooder

parts.words: One who wants not to be a do gooder
parts.note: read as someone whose wants are not for doing good, a person wishing harm on others

explanation.surface: A person who avoids being a busybody charity type.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who wishes harm on others hopes for bad rather than good outcomes.

clue.text: Bigwig looks inside the blockhouse

indicators.note: inside says the letters sit within the words that come before it

explanation.surface: An important person peers inside the fortification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blockhouse' sounds military, but this house is built of blocks of snow.
explanation.definitionFit: An Inuit dome dwelling is made of snow blocks.

clue.text: Judges probably well known to this clerical person

definitions.text: Judges probably well known to this clerical person

parts.words: Judges probably well known to this clerical person
parts.note: Judges is a book of the Old Testament, so the scripture-reading churchman would know it, not courtroom judges

explanation.surface: Magistrates are likely familiar to a certain churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: A priest or minister is a man of the cloth who knows the books of the Bible.

clue.text: Fifty in loan scheme — outcome plain

indicators.note: in means one letter is placed within the others
a scheme here is a fresh arrangement, so the letters of the word loan are reworked

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A fifty-pound loan arrangement has a modest result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scheme' turns LOAN into LANO, and 'in' puts L inside it after the first L.
explanation.definitionFit: A llano is a broad treeless grassland of South America, a flat open expanse.

clue.text: Bowling perhaps at ring for fruit

parts.note: Tom Bowling is the sailor of an old sea song, so a Tom
taken as written
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A bowler takes aim at a target to win a prize of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom Bowling' is a famous English sea ballad by Charles Dibdin, so Bowling is a surname for a Tom.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically a tomato is a fruit, a seed-bearing berry.

clue.text: Balloon provided for a treat, so blow it up

indicators.note: blowing something up shatters it, so the letters of the words before are scattered and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A party balloon bought as a treat, which you should then inflate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blow it up' looks like an instruction to inflate the balloon but is the anagram signal on A TREAT SO.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerostat is any lighter-than-air craft such as a hot-air or gas-filled airship.
